📄 Enemy suffered heavy blows in war against Iran: Army chief

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Chief Commander of Iran’s Army Major General Abdolrahim Mousavi says the war has entered a sensitive and decisive phase, stressing that despite Iran’s victory and the heavy blows inflicted on the aggressor, the country must remain prepared for new aggression.

Speaking Sunday at the first National Iranian Soldier Festival, held during Sacred Defense Week, Hatami said the eight-year war imposed by Iraq’s toppled Baathist regime showed the importance of defending the homeland under the banner of independence.
​
He stressed that the enemy’s credibility is rapidly eroding, saying its increasingly desperate rhetoric reflects confusion over how to confront Iran’s 90-million-strong nation, whose people all consider themselves defenders of their homeland. He added that US President Donald Trump’s promised “help” had amounted to what Iran has witnessed, while he now labels the Iranian people terrorists.
​
He said Lieutenant General Abdolrahim Mousavi, the late commander of the Islamic Republic of Iran Army, after holding senior military and national positions, chose to be identified as an Iranian soldier. Hatami also recalled Lieutenant General Qassem Soleimani’s wish to have Soldier Qassem Soleimani written on his gravestone.
​
Hatami said the enemy had wrongly calculated that killing Iran’s top officials and commanders would cause the Islamic Republic to collapse. Instead, he said, commanders continued to stand their ground and defend the country.
​
The war is not over, Hatami said, adding that Iran had won but must preserve that victory. He warned that the adversary should expect further strikes.
​
He rejected plans to destabilize Iran through pressure and internal conflict, saying Iranians understood the adversary’s intentions.
​
Addressing neighboring and regional countries, Hatami said cooperation with the United States had not brought security and argued that regional security should be ensured by countries of the region.
​
He also described the Strait of Hormuz as a symbol of Iran’s dignity and honor, saying Iran would not allow adversaries to use the strategic waterway while depriving Iranians of its benefits.

📄 President Pezeshkian hails Iran-Turkmenistan ties, hopes for closer cooperation

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian has congratulated Turkmenistan’s national leader and president on their country’s Independence Day, expressing hope that bilateral relations will further expand in line with the interests of both nations.

The president sent separate congratulatory messages to Turkmenistan’s National Leader Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow and President Serdar Berdimuhamedow on Sunday, September 27, marking the 35th anniversary of the Central Asian country’s independence.
​
“The Islamic Republic of Iran and Turkmenistan have always enjoyed fruitful cooperation based on mutual interests and the goodwill of the two countries’ senior officials. I am confident that this cooperation, rooted in the kinship ties between the two nations, will be further strengthened and expanded in the future for the benefit of both peoples,” Pezeshkian said in his message to Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow.
​
In his message to President Berdimuhamedow, Pezeshkian also praised the “deep historical, religious, and civilizational commonalities, as well as the shared borders of friendship” between Iran and Turkmenistan, saying they have helped strengthen and expand beneficial cooperation between the two countries.
​
“I firmly believe that these commonalities and friendship will continue to pave the way for the further development of bilateral relations in the future,” the Iranian president said.

🎙 St. Petersburg university seeks to establish Persian language department

📌 St. Petersburg, IRNA – The rector of Saint Petersburg State Institute of Culture has expressed the university’s interest in establishing a Persian language department, as Iranian Culture Minister Abbas Salehi visited the institution during his trip to Russia.

Salehi, who is in Russia to attend events marking the Days of Iranian Culture, the International Forum of United Cultures, and to hold talks with his Russian counterpart, stressed the need to activate the potential for expanding cultural cooperation between Tehran and Moscow.
​
Alexander Turgayev, rector of Saint Petersburg State Institute of Culture, said the university, which was founded in 1918, has trained numerous prominent figures in Russian culture and arts.
​
Turgayev described Iran’s culture, art and civilization as very rich and recalled becoming familiar with Iranian cinema during his childhood after watching The Leopard of Mazandaran, saying he has developed a strong interest in Iranian culture and civilization.
​
He also noted that the university currently teaches six foreign languages and reiterated its interest in establishing a Persian language department.
​
Salehi welcomed the proposal and instructed Iran’s cultural attaché in Russia to pursue the establishment of the Persian language department in coordination with the Russian side.

⚡️ Iran’s handball goalkeeper signs with Athinaikos H.C.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Zahra Afshari, a promising 19-year-old goalkeeper for Iran’s national handball program, has signed a one-year contract with the Greek club Athinaikos H.C.

Athinaikos ranks among the notable clubs in the Greek Handball League and, in the coming season, will compete not only on the domestic front but also in the 2026–2027 European Cup.
​
The team, however, has started the season poorly, suffering a defeat in its opening match and sitting in 11th place in the 12-team table of the Greek Handball Super League.
​
Afshari, who is 19 years old, played an important role last year, with her standout performances in Iran's youth handball team in the country’s championship at the Bahrain Youth Asian Games, making history with the team and winning the gold medal of that competition.
